blocks.orig: Some people call Kitulo National Park the “Garden of God”. It is one of the leading nature reserves in Africa and has mountain meadows and forests. The Kitulo Plateau is located in the southern highlands of Tanzania. It is the first national park in tropical Africa that was established primarily to protect its flora. This park is the reason why true nature lovers especially make a Tanzania travel.
blocks.html: Kitulo National Park is sometimes referred to as the “Garden of God”. With its mountain meadows and forests it ranks among the leading nature reserves in Africa. The Kitulo Plateau lies in the southern highlands of Tanzania, and it was the first national park in tropical Africa set up mainly to protect plant life. For real nature lovers this park alone is reason enough to go on a Tanzania travel.

blocks.orig: Botanists call the Kitulo Plateau the “Serengeti of Flowers” because it is home to one of the largest flower deposits in the world. In total around 400 plant species live in the montane grasslands. The plateau has more than 45 species of orchids, geophytes, aloes, proteas, geraniums, giant lobelia, lilies and aster daisies and other afro-alpine plants. These mountain meadows are florishing during the rainy season from November to April. You can find many species only in the Kipengere Mountains and the nearby highlands. Brachystelma kituloensis, Impatiens rosulata, and Pterygodium Ukingense can only be found in the Kitulo National Park.
blocks.html: Among botanists the Kitulo Plateau is known as the “Serengeti of Flowers”, as it holds one of the largest concentrations of flowers anywhere in the world. Roughly 400 plant species grow in its montane grasslands. On the plateau you find over 45 species of orchids, along with geophytes, aloes, proteas, geraniums, giant lobelia, lilies, aster daisies and other afro-alpine plants. The mountain meadows are in full bloom during the rainy season from November to April. Many of these species grow only in the Kipengere Mountains and the surrounding highlands, and Brachystelma kituloensis, Impatiens rosulata and Pterygodium Ukingense occur nowhere else but Kitulo National Park.

blocks.orig: Internationally, the flower trade in orchids is large. However, the threat to Kitulo’s orchids came from a different source. In the culture of many ethnic groups the harvest of orchid bulbs for food has a long history. They prepare a dish, known as Chikanda or Kinaka, which is similar to a meatless sausage. After the harvest, they dry the tubers. Then they beat and cook them. Originally a rural delicacy, it was eaten more often in increasing quantities and the gathering of orchids for commercial purposes grew dramatically. This trade was a serious risk to orchids in the southern highlands. Because of it, the plateau became a protected national park. Many visitors also come to Kitulo Plateau national park because  its vast abundance of wildflowers, birds, and grass-eating mammals.
blocks.html: Worldwide there is a big trade in orchids as flowers, yet the danger to Kitulo’s orchids came from elsewhere. Many ethnic groups have a long tradition of digging up orchid bulbs for food. From them they make a dish called Chikanda or Kinaka, something like a meat-free sausage: the tubers are dried after harvesting, then pounded and cooked. What started as a rural delicacy was eaten more and more, in ever greater quantities, and the commercial collecting of orchids rose sharply. This put the orchids of the southern highlands at serious risk, and that is why the plateau was declared a protected national park. Plenty of visitors are also drawn to Kitulo Plateau National Park by its huge wealth of wildflowers, birds and grazing mammals.

blocks.orig: Wildlife in Kitulo Plateau National Park
blocks.html: Animals in Kitulo Plateau National Park

blocks.orig: Except for a few mountain reedbucks and eland, the occurrence of large animals in Kitulo is not very large. But plants, birds and butterflies make up for life in the park. The rare chimpanzee, blue swallow, red chalk hawk, njembe stalksinger, kipengere seedeater, mountain swamp widow, zebra, kipunji monkey, chameleon, lizards, frogs, spiders and other small insects are native to the park.
blocks.html: Apart from a handful of mountain reedbuck and eland, large mammals are fairly scarce in Kitulo. Plants, birds and butterflies more than compensate for that. Native to the park are the rare chimpanzee, blue swallow, red chalk hawk, njembe stalksinger, kipengere seedeater, mountain swamp widow, zebra, kipunji monkey, chameleon, lizards, frogs, spiders and a range of other small insects.

blocks.orig: Activities in Kitulo Plateau National Park
blocks.html: What to do in Kitulo Plateau National Park

blocks.orig: It is possible to take a nice hike, as the park provides great opportunities to take close-up pictures of the magnificent flora and to watch birds from close.
blocks.html: A pleasant hike is very much an option here: the park gives you excellent chances to photograph the splendid flora up close and to observe birds from a short distance.

blocks.orig: Best time to visit Kitulo Plateau National Park
blocks.html: When to go to Kitulo Plateau National Park

blocks.orig: Travelers should plan to visit Kitulo during the months of December through April. This is the rainy season for most of Tanzania, but it is the best time to visit Kitulo Plateau National Park for experiencing the abundance and array of flora.
blocks.html: If you can, plan your visit to Kitulo between December and April. For most of Tanzania that is the rainy season, yet for Kitulo Plateau National Park it is exactly the right moment to see the flora at its richest and most varied.

blocks.orig: The Kitulo National Park, also known as the “Garden of God”, is one of the leading nature reserves in Africa and consists of mountain meadows and forests on the Kitulo Plateau in the southern highlands of Tanzania. The plateau, known by botanists as the “Serengeti of Flowers”, is home to one of the largest flower deposits in the world.
blocks.html: Nicknamed the “Garden of God”, Kitulo National Park ranks among Africa’s foremost nature reserves: a landscape of alpine meadows and woodland on the Kitulo Plateau in the south of Tanzania. Botanists have dubbed the plateau the “Serengeti of Flowers”, since it holds one of the richest collections of flowering plants anywhere on earth.
